bullets.section: Experiment of the week -- Fixing Gollum feet —
bullets.title: simple white vinegar bath
bullets.note:
for my vulture claw-like feet (2:1 ratio, so 2 cups of water for every cup of
vinegar). Ever since judo in Japan at age 15, I’ve had rather disgusting feet.
Athlete’s foot came first, then a little toe fungus, and once you’ve added on
scar tissue and Flintstone callouses, it’s downright revolting. So… I tried
the bath as something new, 15-20 minutes per night for two nights, all while
watching the show in the next bullet. I put the water and vinegar in a
[Sterilite ID
box](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wXL&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=g&)
and used a pumice stone after each session. After two days, the before-and-
after difference has been somewhat astonishing. I’m not ready for any foot
modeling, but I might get back to “normal” if I do this a few times a week for
a bit. Final results TBD, but it’s very cheap, very easy, and seems very
promising.

bullets.title: Mr. Robot
bullets.note:
is GREAT. I don’t know why it took me this long to watch this series, created
by Sam Esmail
([@samesmail](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wXF&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=Y&)).
So far (I’m on ep 8), the writing is fantastic, and it includes equal doses of
intelligence and hilarity. For me, EPISODE 1 was like watching my own internal
dialogue and neuroses, minus the genius and drug addiction. If you ever think
to yourself “Am I crazy?” this show might make you feel better.  
  
The plot basics: Mr. Robot follows Elliot, a young programmer who works as a
cyber-security engineer by day and a vigilante hacker by night. Elliot finds
himself at a crossroads when the mysterious leader of an underground hacker
group recruits him to destroy the corporation he is paid to protect.

Travel Tip —  
[The Thera Cane
Massager](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wXO&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=B&)
for relieving tightness and aches. Whenever I hit the road, I dismantle this
bad boy and pack it in my suitcase. It hits all the hard-to-reach areas in the
middleback region, and it helps relieve plantar-related foot issues.
